questions.stem: Which of the following represents the skills needed that a Service Mapping administrator or implementer should have? (Choose four.)

options.text: Understanding of XML, Regex, Delimited text, and JSON
Understanding of protocols such as HTTP, TCP, SNMP, SOAP, and REST
Scripting capabilities with respect to Unix and Windows commands
Intermediate or above Windows and Unix administration skills
Sufficient skills to build an enterprise web site

questions.explanation: A Service Mapping administrator needs four key skill areas: (A) understanding XML, Regex, Delimited text, and JSON for parsing discovery data; (B) protocol knowledge including HTTP, TCP, SNMP, SOAP, and REST for understanding communication methods; (C) scripting capabilities for Unix and Windows commands used in discovery patterns; and (D) intermediate+ Windows and Unix admin skills for understanding the systems being mapped. Building enterprise web sites (E) and relational database theory (F) are not core SM requirements.

questions.stem: Which one of the following ServiceNow application KPIs would improve most as a direct result of having visibility to a service map created through Service Mapping?

options.text: Problem Management: Number of Incidents per Known Problem
Incident Management: Mean Time to Resolve
Event Management: Signal to Noise Ratio
Change Management: Number of Major Changes

questions.explanation: Incident Management Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR) would improve most from service map visibility. Service maps show the complete topology of a service — all CIs, their relationships, and dependencies. When an incident occurs, this visibility allows teams to quickly identify the root cause CI and its impact, dramatically reducing the time to diagnose and resolve issues.

questions.stem: How many ServiceNow instances can one MID Server connect to?
questions.explanation: One MID Server can connect to exactly 1 ServiceNow instance. This is a fundamental architectural constraint — each MID Server is registered to and communicates with a single instance. If you need MID Server connectivity for multiple instances, you must deploy separate MID Servers for each instance. The MID Server's config.xml contains the single instance URL it connects to.

questions.stem: When a Windows Server is reclassified from the Server [cmdb_ci_server] table to the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table, which one of the following describes the process that occurred?
questions.explanation: When a Windows Server is moved from the generic Server [cmdb_ci_server] table to the more specific Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] table, this is called a Class Change. During Discovery, when more specific information is gathered about a CI (e.g., the OS is identified as Windows), the CMDB reclassifies the CI to a more specific child class. The sys_class_name field value changes to reflect the new, more precise classification.

questions.stem: To begin the configuration of tag-based services, tag values must be defined where?
questions.explanation: To begin configuring tag-based services, tag values must be defined in Tag categories. You create tag categories at Service Mapping > Administration > CI Tag Categories. Each tag category groups similar tag keys (e.g., an 'Environment' category containing keys like 'Env', 'env', 'Environment'). Service Mapping then uses these categories when defining tag-based service families. Options B (Tag catalogs), C (Tag-based service families), and D (Tag libraries) are either incorrect terms or later steps in the process.

questions.stem: Which of the following are potential benefits when implementing Service Mapping? (Choose four.)

options.text: Reduced ongoing service map maintenance effort as a result of automated map updates
Faster service issue resolution and reduced downtime due to better root cause analysis
Reduction in effort to create service maps
Reduction in change related incidents due to improved service visibility during change planning
More accurate alerts from monitoring tools

questions.explanation: Service Mapping benefits include: Reduced ongoing maintenance effort from automated map updates (A), Faster issue resolution via better root cause analysis (B), Reduction in effort to create service maps through automation (D), and Reduction in change-related incidents due to improved service visibility during change planning (E). Improved SAM capabilities (C) is not a direct SM benefit since SM focuses on service topology, not software licensing. More accurate alerts from monitoring tools (F) is an Event Management benefit, not SM.

questions.stem: Which one of the following can be used to enable patterns to search for additional attributes and modify discovery logic defined in an Identification Section without modifying the baseline pattern and potentially impacting upgrades?

options.text: Add step(s) to the pattern’s Identification Section.
Add step(s) to the pattern’s Connection Section.
Add step(s) to the pattern’s Extension Section.
Add step(s) to the pattern’s Update Set.
Add step(s) directly to the NDL code.

questions.explanation: Extension Sections allow patterns to search for additional attributes and modify discovery logic without modifying the baseline pattern. By adding steps to a pattern's Extension Section, you can customize discovery behavior while preserving the original pattern. This prevents upgrade conflicts because the baseline pattern can be updated during upgrades without overwriting your customizations.

questions.stem: In the image, which one of the following best describes the lower icons?

options.text: The connections from HAProxy are to other CIs that had errors during discovery.
The connections from HAProxy are application clusters.
The connections from HAProxy could not be identified and are marked as a Generic Application.
The connections from HAProxy are marked as boundaries.

questions.explanation: The lower icons likely represent connections from HAProxy to applications that could not be identified and are marked as Generic Application. When Service Mapping discovers connections to processes that don't match any existing process classifier, it labels them as 'Generic Application' CIs. This signals to the administrator that a custom pattern or process classifier needs to be created for those applications. Error connections (A) would show a different icon, clusters (B) have a specific visual, and boundaries (D) represent network limits.

questions.stem:
Assuming Reconciliation Rules (Reconciliation Definitions) were configured exactly the same for both Data Sources, ServiceNow and ServiceWatch, for the Application [cmdb_ci_appl] table and the following Data Source Precedence Rules are configured.
Which one of the following is true?

options.text: If an Application CI is discovered with a Data Source, ServiceNow, then if the same Application CI is discovered by the Data Source, Altiris, an update will be allowed.
If an Application CI is discovered with a Data Source, ServiceWatch, then if the same Application CI is discovered by the Data Source, ServiceNow, an update will be allowed.
If an Application CI is discovered with a Data Source, ServiceNow, then if the same Application CI is discovered by the Data Source, ServiceWatch, an update will be allowed.
If an Application CI is discovered with a Data Source, ServiceWatch, then if the same Application CI is discovered by the Data Source, Altiris, an update will be allowed.

questions.explanation: With Data Source Precedence Rules configured, if an Application CI is first discovered by ServiceNow and then the same CI is discovered by ServiceWatch, an update will be allowed. Data Source Precedence controls which data source can overwrite another. When ServiceWatch has higher precedence than ServiceNow in the Reconciliation Definitions for the same table, ServiceWatch data can update existing ServiceNow-discovered CIs. Options A, B, and D describe scenarios that would be blocked by the configured precedence hierarchy.

questions.stem: Service Mapping provides visibility to the Operator in Agent Workspace without leaving the Workspace UI. This visibility includes what items associated with the CI? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Service Mapping provides visibility to the Operator in Agent Workspace for Incidents (C) and Alerts (D) associated with CIs in the service map. Operators can see active incidents and alerts on mapped CIs without leaving the Agent Workspace UI, enabling faster troubleshooting. Releases (A) are not typically surfaced in the Agent Workspace service map view. Problems (B) while related to CIs are not part of the standard SM visibility provided to operators in Agent Workspace.

questions.stem: In ServiceNow Discovery, which one of the following phases is the server RAM value discovered?
questions.explanation: In ServiceNow Discovery, server RAM is discovered during the Identification and Exploration phases. The Exploration phase runs probes that collect detailed hardware information including RAM, CPU, disk, installed software, and other attributes. Discovery proceeds through these phases sequentially: Port Scan (finds open ports) → Classification (determines device type using port fingerprint) → Identification (determines unique CI) → Exploration (collects detailed attributes like RAM). RAM is not collected during Port Scan (A) or Classification (B).

questions.stem: In Pattern Designer, which one of the following best describes the Create Connection step?

options.text: Provides information about integrations to the host
Provides information about relationships between cluster members
Provides information about outbound connections to other CIs
Provides information about relationships between the host and installed software

questions.explanation: In Pattern Designer, the Create Connection step provides information about outbound connections to other CIs. This step defines relationships from the discovered CI to other CIs it communicates with or depends on. It creates the CI relationships (like 'Runs on', 'Connects to') that form the service map topology by discovering and recording outbound connections from the host CI.

questions.stem: Which one of the following best describes the definition of an Entry Point?

options.text: A method by which a user interacts with a service or a CI interacts with another CI
A type of communication taking place between applications
A template of attributes that define a communication type between applications
A Host::Hosted on relation between CIs

questions.explanation: An Entry Point in Service Mapping is a method by which a user interacts with a service or a CI interacts with another CI. Entry points define the access point to a service — typically a URL, IP address and port, or protocol-based endpoint that Service Mapping uses as a starting point for discovering the service. Option B describes a protocol/connection type, not an entry point. Option C describes a connection type template. Option D describes a CI relationship type (Hosted on), not an entry point.

questions.stem: In Service Mapping, when discovery is started, what is the execution strategy used to run Identification Sections?

options.text: Identification Sections are executed randomly until one is successful and if more than one section is successful an error will be displayed.
Identification Sections are executed randomly and the data gathered by the successful sections are merged.
Identification Sections are executed one by one in the order they are listed and the last section that is successful will be used.
Identification Sections are executed one by one in the order they are listed until the first successful match which concludes the Identification phase.

questions.explanation: Identification Sections in a Service Mapping pattern are executed one by one in the order they are listed until the first successful match, which concludes the Identification phase. Once a section successfully identifies the CI (matching attributes like class, configuration file, etc.), remaining sections are skipped. This ordered, first-match approach ensures deterministic identification. Sections are NOT executed randomly (A, B), and it's the first successful match that's used, not the last (C).

questions.stem: Which one of the following Linux commands can be used by a non root user to return the process ID listening on port 8080?
questions.explanation: The command 'sudo netstat -anp | grep :8080' is correct for a non-root Linux user to find a process ID on port 8080. The -a flag shows all connections, -n shows numeric addresses, -p shows the PID/program name (requires elevated privileges). A non-root user needs sudo to see PID information, making option C (without sudo) insufficient. Option A uses '-p TCP' which is a Windows netstat syntax, not Linux. Option D uses '-pid *' which is not a valid netstat flag on Linux.

questions.stem: Which one of the following best describes the process that Service Mapping uses to run a command on a target device?

options.text: Service Mapping provides a task with the command that the MID Server collects, the MID Server executes the command on the target device, and returns the result to the ServiceNow instance in an XML payload.
The MID Server decides what command to execute, executes the command on the target device, and returns the result to the ServiceNow instance in an XML payload.
Service Mapping sends a request to the target device to execute a command, and the target device returns the result to the ServiceNow instance through the MID Server.
Service Mapping sends a request to the target device to execute a command, and the target device returns the result to the ServiceNow instance.

questions.explanation: Service Mapping provides a task with the command to the MID Server, the MID Server executes the command on the target device, and returns the result to the ServiceNow instance in an XML payload. SM uses the MID Server as an intermediary — the instance sends commands to the MID Server via the ECC Queue, the MID Server runs them on the target, and sends results back in XML format. The MID Server doesn't decide what to run (B). The target device doesn't communicate directly with the instance (C, D) — the MID Server acts as the proxy.

questions.stem: In Event Management, which of the following rules allows for automatic task creation?
questions.explanation: In Event Management, Alert Management rules allow for automatic task creation. Alert Management rules define conditions under which alerts automatically create tasks such as incidents. When an alert matches the criteria in an Alert Management rule (severity, CI type, alert type, etc.), the system automatically generates the associated task. Event rules (B) process raw events into alerts. Task rules (C) is not specific to EM. Alert Correlation rules (D) group related alerts together but don't create tasks.

questions.stem:
During ServiceNow Discovery, which one of the following is the approximate number of host IPs that are port scanned with a Discovery Schedule configured with an IP network as shown?
180.181.0.0/16
questions.explanation: A /16 subnet mask means the first 16 bits are the network portion, leaving 16 bits for host addresses. This yields 2^16 = 65,536 IP addresses, approximately 65 thousand. The network 180.181.0.0/16 covers the range 180.181.0.0 to 180.181.255.255. Options A (~5 million), B (~1 million), and D (~500,000) are significantly larger and correspond to larger CIDR ranges like /10, /12, or /13 respectively.

questions.stem: ServiceNow only needs Domain user with local admin rights to discover Windows hosts as part of a successful implementation of ServiceNow Discovery, however which of the following targets will not be discovered?
questions.explanation: With only a Domain user with local admin rights, Windows Domain Controller Servers will NOT be discovered properly. Domain Controllers require specific elevated privileges beyond local admin, such as domain admin or enterprise admin rights, because they manage Active Directory services with restricted access. Standard domain user with local admin can discover regular Windows hosts (A, B, D) including AD member servers, DHCP servers, and DNS servers, but Domain Controllers have additional security restrictions.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for variables defined in an Identification Section?

options.text: Identification Section variables can also be used in all other Identification Sections in any pattern.
Identification Section variables can also be used in Parent CI Types.
Identification Section variables can also be used in all other Identification Sections in the same pattern.
Identification Section variables can also be used in Connection Sections for any pattern.
Identification Section variables can also be used in Connection Sections for the same pattern.

questions.explanation: Identification Section variables can be used in Connection Sections for the same pattern. Variables defined in an Identification Section of a pattern are scoped to that pattern and available to Connection Sections within it. This allows data gathered during identification (like paths, ports, or configuration values) to be reused when discovering connections. They cannot be used across different patterns (A, D) or in parent CI types (B). Option C is wrong because other Identification Sections in the same pattern cannot reuse them across sections.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best explains the following URL: https://<Instance_URL>/SaCmdManager.do?ip=198.51.100.66?

options.text: The user is starting the Command Line Console and is able to send commands to the host 198.51.100.66.
The user is starting the Command Line Console and explicitly directs Service Mapping to use the MID Server 198.51.100.66 to execute commands.
This is not a valid URL for Service Mapping.
The user is starting the Command Line Console and is able to send commands against the ServiceNow instance at 198.51.100.66.

questions.explanation: The URL SaCmdManager.do?ip=198.51.100.66 starts the Service Mapping Command Line Console targeting host 198.51.100.66. This tool allows administrators to manually send discovery commands to a specific host for testing and troubleshooting pattern execution. The ip parameter specifies the target host to execute commands against. It's not directing to a specific MID Server (B) — the MID Server selection is handled separately. It is a valid SM URL (C is wrong). The IP refers to the target host, not the ServiceNow instance (D).

questions.stem: In Service Mapping, which one of the following is true if a target host is already discovered and in the CMDB?

options.text: The host will be deleted in the CMDB and a new host record will be created during Service Mapping discovery.
The host will be immediately rediscovered, but only the changes will be updated in the CMDB during Service Mapping discovery.
The host will be immediately rediscovered and updated in the CMDB during Service Mapping discovery.
The host will not be rediscovered during Service Mapping discovery.

questions.explanation: If a target host is already discovered and exists in the CMDB, Service Mapping will immediately rediscover the host and update its record in the CMDB. SM always runs fresh discovery on the target and updates whichever attributes have changed. The existing CI is not deleted and recreated (A). SM doesn't do partial updates based on changes only (B) — it rediscovers fully. And it does not skip already-discovered hosts (D) — it rediscovers them to ensure the map is current.

questions.stem: In Service Mapping, when discovery is started, what is the execution strategy used to run Connection Sections?

options.text: Connection Sections are executed one by one and connections will result from each successful section.
Connection Sections are executed randomly and connections will result from each successful section.
Connection Sections are executed one by one in the order they are listed until the first successful section.
Connection Sections are executed one by one in the order they are listed with a connection created from the last successful section.

questions.explanation: Connection Sections are executed one by one and connections result from each successful section. Unlike Identification Sections (which stop at first match), ALL Connection Sections run because a CI can have multiple different types of connections. Each successful Connection Section creates its respective connections in the service map. Sections are NOT executed randomly (B). They don't stop at first success (C) — all sections run. And connections come from every successful section, not just the last (D).

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a public IP Address?
questions.explanation: 225.16.0.5 is the only address that is not in a private IP range. The three private IP ranges are: 10.0.0.0/8 (10.x.x.x), 172.16.0.0/12 (172.16-31.x.x), and 192.168.0.0/16 (192.168.x.x). 172.20.5.9 (A) falls in the 172.16-31 private range, 192.168.100.100 (C) is in the 192.168 range, and 10.0.6.8 (D) is in the 10.x range. While 225.16.0.5 is technically a multicast address (224-239 range), it is the only non-private address among the options.

questions.stem: Given the CMDB class structure shown, which types of Configuration Items (CIs) will be included in a report run against the Server [cmdb_ci_server] table?

options.text: CIs defined directly in Server [cmdb_ci_server] table and all parent classes
CIs defined directly in Server [cmdb_ci_server] table and all child classes
CIs defined directly in the Server [cmdb_ci_server] table

questions.explanation: A report run against the Server [cmdb_ci_server] table will include CIs defined directly in the Server table AND all child (extended) classes. ServiceNow table inheritance means queries on a parent table automatically include records from all tables that extend it (e.g., Linux Server, Windows Server, ESX Server). This is a fundamental CMDB behavior. The report would NOT include parent classes (A) since inheritance goes downward only. It won't be limited to just the Server table itself (C) without child records.

questions.stem:
Which one of the following best represents the output from the following Regular Expression?
([\w\d\-\.]+)

options.text: Match a single character in the list between one and unlimited times.
Match a single character in the list one time.
Match a single character in the list between one and three times.
Match a single character in the list between one and ten times.

questions.explanation: The regex ([\w\d\-\.]+) matches a single character from the character class [\w\d\-\.] (word characters, digits, hyphens, and dots) one or more times (unlimited). The + quantifier means 'match between one and unlimited times' (at least once, no upper limit). Option B (one time) would be [\w\d\-\.] without the +. Option C (one to three times) would use {1,3}. Option D (one to ten times) would use {1,10}. The + is greedy and matches as many characters as possible.

questions.stem: Which one of the following describes how a MID Server communicates with a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: A MID Server communicates with a ServiceNow instance by initiating connections on HTTPS. The MID Server always initiates the communication outbound — it polls the instance's ECC Queue for work and sends results back. This outbound-only model is a key security feature: no inbound connections from the internet to the MID Server are required, only outbound HTTPS (port 443) from MID to instance.

questions.stem:
Assuming the Apache Web Server Identification Rule (CI Identifier) is configured as shown with the following Criterion attributes:

Class -

Configuration file -

Version -

Yesterday, an Apache Web Server CI was discovered as part of Service Mapping. Today, the application owner upgraded the Apache Web Server to a different version and reran discovery of the service. What will happen in the CMDB?

options.text: A new Apache Web Server CI is created.
The existing Apache Web Server CI will be reconciled with the upgraded Apache Web Server CI and its version will be updated.
The Apache Web Server CI will be reclassified as a Web Server CI.

questions.explanation: The existing Apache Web Server CI will be reconciled with the upgraded version and its version attribute updated. Since the CI Identifier uses Class and Configuration file as criteria (NOT Version), updating the version doesn't change the CI's identity. The same Class + Configuration file combination matches the existing CI, so ServiceNow reconciles and updates the version attribute on the existing record. No duplication error (A) occurs because the identifier still matches. No new CI (B) is created because identity criteria haven't changed. No reclassification (D) occurs.

questions.stem: Within the CMDB, all application CI Types/Classes are children of which parent class?
questions.explanation: All application CI Types/Classes in the CMDB are children of the Application [cmdb_ci_appl] parent class. This is the base class in the CMDB hierarchy for all application-type CIs (web servers, databases, middleware, etc.). Installed Software tracks software installations, Database Instance is a specific app type, Software is for software products, and Licenses track entitlements — none are the parent of all applications.

questions.stem: In Service Mapping, which one of the following best describes the process of discovery after an Entry Point is configured?

options.text: For each pattern that supports the Entry Point Type, run identification Sections until one finishes successfully and then run each Connection Section for the pattern.
For each pattern that supports the Entry Point Type, run all the identification Sections that finish successfully and then run each Connection Section for the pattern.
For each pattern that supports the Entry Point Type, run identification Sections until one finishes successfully and then run Connection Sections until one finishes successfully.
For each pattern that supports the Entry Point Type, run all the Identification Sections and run all Connection Sections.

questions.explanation: After an Entry Point is configured, Service Mapping runs identification Sections until one finishes successfully (first match wins), then runs EACH Connection Section for the matched pattern. Identification is exclusive — only the first successful section determines the CI type. Connection is inclusive — all Connection Sections are executed to discover all outbound relationships. This is a fundamental SM discovery behavior.

questions.stem: When using the Pattern Designer, a Regular Expression parsing strategy is available from which operation?
questions.explanation: In Pattern Designer, a Regular Expression parsing strategy is available from the Parse File operation. Parse File reads configuration files from discovered systems and uses regex patterns to extract specific values (like connection strings, port numbers, hostnames) from file content. Other operations like Set Variable, Match, and Create Connection use different mechanisms for their data handling.

questions.stem:
Using Pattern Designer, which one of the following Delimited Text Parsing Strategies could be used to parse CO from the string?
Location,Denver,CO

options.text: Delimiter of a comma and position 3
Delimiter of a comma and position 2

questions.explanation: Using Delimited Text Parsing with a comma delimiter: 'Location,Denver,CO' splits into position 1: 'Location', position 2: 'Denver', position 3: 'CO'. To extract 'CO', use delimiter comma and position 3. Option B uses 'Location,' as delimiter which would split differently but position 2 wouldn't yield CO. Option C uses 'Denver' as delimiter which is incorrect syntax. Option D uses comma delimiter but position 2 which returns 'Denver', not 'CO'.

questions.stem: In Event Management, if a Message key is not passed from an Event, which of the following Alert fields combine to populate the Message key on an Alert?
questions.explanation: When an Event in Event Management does not pass a Message key, the Alert's Message key is automatically populated from four fields: Source, Node, Type, and Resource. These four fields uniquely identify the nature and location of the alert. This combination ensures that subsequent events from the same source, affecting the same node/resource and of the same type, are correlated into the same alert. Options A, B, and C contain incorrect field combinations (Task, Description, Created, Number are not part of the message key formula).

questions.stem: In Service Mapping, when an application is identified as a Generic application, which one of the following is the cause?

options.text: No Pattern Identification and Connection Section matches

questions.explanation: When an application is identified as a Generic Application in Service Mapping, it means no Pattern Identification Section matched the discovered process. The identification phase tries each pattern's identification sections against the discovered data. If none match, the application defaults to 'Generic Application' — indicating the process was found but couldn't be classified as a specific application type.

questions.stem: Which address is required for Service Mapping to discover a Load Balancer that does not previously exist in the CMDB?
questions.explanation: The Management IP address is required for Service Mapping to discover a Load Balancer that doesn't previously exist in the CMDB. Load balancers have virtual IP addresses that serve traffic but the management IP is the address used for administrative access and discovery communication. The MID Server connects to this management IP to run discovery probes. MAC address (B) is a layer-2 identifier not used for remote discovery. Public IP (C) might be the VIP, not management. MIB address (D) is not a standard SM concept.

questions.stem:
Which one of the following Regular Expressions could be used to parse the value 5.2.0 from the string?
Version 5.2.0
questions.explanation: The regex 'Version\s+(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)' correctly parses '5.2.0' from 'Version 5.2.0'. \s+ matches one or more whitespace characters after 'Version'. The capture group (\d+\.\d+\.\d+) matches three groups of digits separated by literal dots: 5.2.0. Option A 'Version (\..*)' would match '.2.0' (starts with dot). Option C 'Version (\d+)' captures only '5'. Option D has three separate capture groups instead of one, giving ('5','2','0') rather than '5.2.0' as a single value.

questions.stem: Which of the following reasons would a prospect consider purchasing ServiceNow Event Management? (Choose three.)

options.text: Determine impacted services from a given event/alert.
Provide software deployment capabilities to patch problem infrastructure.
Automatically generate incidents for certain classes of alerts.
Provide state of the art monitoring capabilities across a wide array of different types of infrastructure.
Consolidate events from disparate monitoring tools into a consolidated central system.

questions.explanation: Prospects would purchase Event Management to: Determine impacted services from events/alerts (A) — EM correlates alerts to service maps to show service impact; Automatically generate incidents for certain alert classes (C) — Alert Management rules automate incident creation; Consolidate events from disparate monitoring tools (E) — EM aggregates events from multiple monitoring sources into a centralized console. Software deployment (B) is handled by change/release management. EM does NOT provide monitoring capabilities itself (D) — it consumes events from existing monitoring tools.

questions.stem:
When running Service Mapping discovery, which of the following represents the root cause of the error?
“Failed to access target system. Access is denied”
questions.explanation: The error 'Failed to access target system. Access is denied' indicates a Windows authentication error. This message appears when the credentials provided for Windows discovery fail to authenticate against the target system. It means the MID Server could not log in to the Windows host using the configured credentials. SSO authentication (A) is not used in pattern discovery. CLI permissions (B) would show a different error message. Applicative permissions (C) would succeed in logging in but fail on specific commands, not with 'Access is denied'.

questions.stem: Which one of the following ECC Queue records contains the XML payload returned from the MID Server that will be processed by the ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: The ECC Queue record containing the XML payload returned from the MID Server is an Input record with Ready state. 'Input' means data coming into the ServiceNow instance (from MID Server). 'Ready' means the record is ready to be processed by the instance. The flow: Instance creates Output/Ready → MID picks up → MID processes → MID creates Input/Ready with results. Input/Pending (A) is not a standard state for results. Output records (C, D) are commands sent TO the MID Server, not results coming back.

questions.stem:
Assume an Apache Web Server Identifier Entry is configured as shown:

If the Apache Web Server Discovery Pattern has a step configured to collect the Configuration file data but NOT configured with a step to collect the Version information, what will happen when executing a Service Mapping discovery?

options.text: The Apache Web Server CI will be reclassified as a Web Server CI.
The Apache Web Server configuration item will be discovered successfully and either inserted or updated in the CMDB.

questions.explanation: The Apache Web Server CI will be discovered successfully and either inserted or updated in the CMDB. If the Identifier Entry uses Class and Configuration file as criteria but NOT Version, then a pattern that collects the Configuration file (but not Version) still provides enough data for successful identification. The CI is identified by its Class + Config file, and version is simply a non-identifying attribute. No identification error (A) or duplication error (D) occurs. No reclassification (B) happens since the Class is properly identified.

questions.stem: Which one of the following describes when the MID Server config.xml file is read and used?
questions.explanation: The MID Server's config.xml file is read and used when the MID Server application starts. At startup, the MID Server reads config.xml to load its configuration parameters including instance URL, credentials, name, and various settings. Changes to config.xml require a MID Server restart to take effect. The file is not read on save (A, B) — merely editing the file doesn't trigger the MID Server to reload. It is read at startup (D), not shutdown (C).

questions.stem: In Service Mapping, which one of the following must be available or created in advance, in order to be able to create a Discovery Pattern?
questions.explanation: To create a Discovery Pattern, a CI Type/Table must be available or created in advance. Every pattern maps discovered resources to a specific CI class in the CMDB. Without a target CI Type, there's nowhere to store the discovered configuration items. Process Classifiers, Identification Rules, and Application Services can be created later, but the CI class must exist first as the foundation for the pattern.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a valid format when entering SSH Private Key credentials?
questions.explanation: PEM (Privacy Enhanced Mail) is the valid format for entering SSH Private Key credentials in ServiceNow. PEM is the standard encoding format for SSH keys, recognized by its BEGIN/END markers (e.g., -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----). PGP is for encryption/signing, PDP and PMI are unrelated to SSH key formats.

questions.stem: Which one of the following best describes what will happen if Discovery is configured with 3 MID Servers in a Load Balance Cluster with Shazzam cluster support disabled?

options.text: All three MID Servers will be used during the Port Scan phase and all three will be used during the classification phase.
Only one MID Server will be used during the Identification phase and all three will be used during the exploration phase.
Only one MID Server will be used during the Port Scan phase and all three will be used during the classification phase.
All three MID Server will be used during the Identification phase and only one will be used during the exploration phase.

questions.explanation: With 3 MID Servers in a Load Balance Cluster and Shazzam cluster support disabled, only one MID Server performs the Port Scan phase while all three are used during the Classification phase. When Shazzam (the distributed port scanning feature) is disabled, port scanning is not distributed and falls to a single MID Server. questions.explanation: In the Discovery Log, the green S represents a step in an Identification Section of a pattern. Green indicates the step executed successfully. The Discovery Log uses color-coded letters to show the status of pattern execution: green for successful steps, red for failures. The 'S' specifically denotes an individual step within the identification process of a discovery pattern.

questions.stem: In Service Mapping, which one of the following icons represents a credential error on the Service map?
questions.explanation: In Service Mapping, a yellow triangle icon on the service map represents a credential error. This warning indicator appears when Service Mapping cannot authenticate to a discovered CI due to missing, incorrect, or expired credentials. The question mark icon indicates an unidentified CI (Generic Application), while the red stop sign indicates a more severe error like an unreachable host.

questions.stem: Which of the following are methods used to initiate discovery on a service? (Choose three.)

options.text: Map multiple services suggested by Service Mapping by discovering the load balancers in an enterprise.
Map multiple services by importing entry points from a CSV file.
Map a single service defined by configuring an entry point.
Map services suggested by the discovery of MID Servers in an enterprise.
Map services based on Assets stored in the CMDB.

questions.explanation: The three methods to initiate service discovery are: Map multiple services suggested by discovering load balancers in an enterprise (A) — discovers LBs to suggest services behind them; Map multiple services by importing entry points from a CSV file (B) — bulk import of service entry points; Map a single service by configuring an entry point (C) — manual single-service mapping. MID Server discovery (D) discovers MID Servers, not services. Asset-based mapping from CMDB (E) is not a standard SM discovery initiation method.

questions.stem: In Service Mapping, which one of the following can be useful in determining which Patterns, Identification Sections, Connection Sections, and Steps are tried?
questions.explanation: The Discovery Log is used to determine which Patterns, Identification Sections, Connection Sections, and Steps were tried during Service Mapping discovery. It provides a detailed trace of the entire discovery process — showing which patterns were evaluated, which sections succeeded or failed, and which individual steps were executed, making it the primary troubleshooting tool for Service Mapping.

questions.stem: Which one of the following represents what the MID stands for in MID Server?
questions.explanation: MID stands for Management, Instrumentation, and Discovery. The MID Server performs three core functions: Management of configuration data and automation tasks, Instrumentation for monitoring and collecting data from infrastructure, and Discovery of CIs and their relationships in the network. These three capabilities define the server's role as the bridge between the ServiceNow instance and customer infrastructure.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the most common risk that can negatively impact a Service Mapping engagement?

options.text: The customer external firewall does not meet the requirements needed for the Service Mapping MID Server to communicate with their ServiceNow Instance.
MID server resource requirements are beyond capacity of the customer.
Customer security team is not made aware early enough in the engagement of the credential requirements.
Customer is not using Active Directory for credential authentication.

questions.explanation: The most common risk that negatively impacts a Service Mapping engagement is the customer security team not being made aware early enough of the credential requirements. SM requires extensive credentials across many systems (Windows, Linux, databases, cloud providers, load balancers, etc.), and security team delays in provisioning these credentials is the biggest bottleneck. External firewalls (A) are typically addressed during MID Server setup. MID Server resources (B) are usually adequate. Active Directory (D) is not required but commonly used.

questions.stem: A defined relationship between two Configuration Items (CIs), such as Runs on, Depends On, or Contains is called a what?
questions.explanation: A defined relationship between two Configuration Items (CIs), such as 'Runs on', 'Depends On', or 'Contains', is called a Relationship Type. Relationship Types are stored in the cmdb_rel_type table and define the semantic meaning of connections between CIs. Each relationship type has a parent descriptor (e.g., 'Runs on') and a child descriptor (e.g., 'Runs'), creating bidirectional relationship definitions.

questions.stem: Which of the following are benefits a service map can bring during an Incident resolution? (Choose three.)

options.text: Quickly identifies any recent incidents that occurred on components of the impacted service.
Narrows down possible affected components when a service is impacted.
Helps reduce the number of unplanned changes in a customer environment.
Helps pinpoint code errors after a faulty application is identified.
Quickly identifies any recent changes performed on components of the impacted service.

questions.explanation: Service maps help during Incident resolution by: Quickly identifying recent incidents on impacted service components (A), Narrowing down possible affected components when a service is impacted (B), and Quickly identifying recent changes performed on components (E) — change visibility is critical for root cause analysis. Reducing unplanned changes (C) is a change management benefit, not incident resolution. Pinpointing code errors (D) is application debugging, which service maps don't provide.

questions.stem: Which one of the following in the CMDB Identification and Reconciliation application allows a CMDB administrator to specify authorized data sources that can update a CMDB table or a set of table attributes?
questions.explanation: Datasource Precedence Rules in the CMDB Identification and Reconciliation application allow administrators to specify authorized data sources that can update a CMDB table or set of table attributes. These rules define which data sources (Discovery, Service Mapping, imports, etc.) have authority over specific CI attributes, controlling which source wins when multiple sources attempt to update the same data.

questions.stem: You have run Service Mapping discovery against a customer service and discovered the CI in the image. The customer indicates that Apache should have an outgoing connection to Tomcat. Which one of the following could be the issue?

options.text: No Connection Section is defined for Apache to Tomcat.
No Tomcat CI Type is defined.
No Identification Rule is defined for Tomcat.
Credentials are not configured for Tomcat.

questions.explanation: If Apache should have an outgoing connection to Tomcat but it doesn't appear on the service map, the most likely cause is that no Connection Section is defined for Apache to Tomcat. Connection Sections in discovery patterns define outbound relationships between CIs. Without a Connection Section specifying how Apache connects to Tomcat (e.g., via TCP port), the relationship won't be discovered even if both CIs exist.

questions.stem: After discovering load balancers in a customer environment, service candidates may appear on the Service Mapping Home page under which one of the following tiles?
questions.explanation: After discovering load balancers in a customer environment, service candidates appear on the Service Mapping Home page under the Review tile. Service candidates are suggested application services that need administrator review before they become active service instances. The administrator reviews candidates to accept or reject them. Map (A) is where you configure mapping. Fix (B) shows issues to resolve. Approve (C) is not a standard SM tile. Completed (D) shows finished maps.

questions.stem: Which one of the following best represents the breadth of types of Configuration Items (CIs) discovered by running Service Mapping?
questions.explanation: Service Mapping discovers Cloud Services, Applications, and CI Relationships, representing the broadest scope of what SM maps. SM's primary purpose is discovering application services — the applications, cloud components, and relationships between them that make up a service. Hardware and Network Gear (A) are primarily Discovery outputs. Physical/Logical/Certificates (B) is incomplete. Licenses and IP addresses (C) are not SM's focus. Hardware/Licenses/Relationships (E) mixes Discovery (hardware) with SAM (licenses).

questions.stem: When building a Discovery Pattern, which one of the following operations results in a termination of the Identification or Connection Section if a condition is not met?
questions.explanation: The Match operation results in a termination of the Identification or Connection Section if a condition is not met. Match acts as a gate/checkpoint — it evaluates a condition against discovered data, and if the condition fails, the entire section stops executing. This is how patterns quickly eliminate non-matching identification paths without running unnecessary subsequent steps.

questions.stem: Which of the following are created automatically when using the map option Create pattern from generic application?

Identification Rule, CI Class/Class, Identification Section

questions.explanation: When using 'Create pattern from generic application', three items are automatically created: a Discovery Pattern (the pattern to discover this application type), a CI Type/Class (a new CMDB class for this application), and a Process Classifier (to identify the process in future discoveries). These three components work together to define, identify, and discover the new application type. Options B, C, and D include Identification Rule or Identification Section, which are components within a pattern but are not separately auto-created as standalone records.

When using a Delimited Text Parsing Strategy, what delimiter and position will parse 2014 from the string?
2014/02/07-17:49:36
questions.explanation: Using Delimited Text Parsing with '/' as the delimiter, '2014/02/07-17:49:36' splits into position 1: '2014', position 2: '02', position 3: '07-17:49:36'. To parse '2014', use delimiter '/' and position 1. Option A (space delimiter) wouldn't find '2014' since the string has no spaces. Option B uses position 0, but ServiceNow Delimited Text positions are 1-based. Option D uses '2014' as delimiter which would split differently.

questions.stem: In Service Mapping, which one of the following best describes the process of discovery after an Entry Point is configured?

options.text: For each pattern that supports the Entry Point Type, run all the Identification Sections and run all Extension Sections.
For each pattern that supports the Entry Point Type, run Identification Sections until one finishes successfully and then run all Extension Sections for the pattern.
For each pattern that supports the Entry Point Type, run all the Identification Sections that finish successfully and then run each Extension Section for the pattern.
For each pattern that supports the Entry Point Type, run Identification Sections until one finishes successfully and then run Extensions Sections until one finishes successfully.

questions.explanation: After an Entry Point is configured, for each pattern supporting that Entry Point Type, Service Mapping runs Identification Sections until one finishes successfully, then runs all Extension Sections for the pattern. This matches the ID section execution strategy (first-match stops) combined with Extensions which all run (similar to Connection Sections). Option A is wrong because not all ID sections run. Options C and D incorrectly describe the ID section behavior or Extension section behavior.
